Abraham obeyed, bound Isaac on the altar, and raised the knife, but the angel of the LORD stopped him and provided a ram caught in a thicket instead. God swore to bless Abraham and multiply his seed because he had not withheld his only son.

verses.kjv: And Sarah was an hundred and seven and twenty years old: these were the years of the life of Sarah.
verses.modern: Sarah lived 127 years; these were the years of the life of Sarah.

verses.kjv: And Sarah died in Kirjatharba; the same is Hebron in the land of Canaan: and Abraham came to mourn for Sarah, and to weep for her.
verses.modern: Sarah died in Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan, and Abraham went in to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her.

verses.kjv: And Abraham stood up from before his dead, and spake unto the sons of Heth, saying,
verses.modern: Then Abraham rose up from before his dead and spoke to the sons of Heth, saying,

verses.kjv: I am a stranger and a sojourner with you: give me a possession of a buryingplace with you, that I may bury my dead out of my sight.
verses.modern: 'I am a stranger and a sojourner among you. Give me property for a burying place with you, that I may bury my dead out of my sight.'

verses.kjv: And the children of Heth answered Abraham, saying unto him,
verses.modern: The sons of Heth answered Abraham, saying to him,

verses.kjv: Hear us, my lord: thou art a mighty prince among us: in the choice of our sepulchres bury thy dead; none of us shall withhold from thee his sepulchre, but that thou mayest bury thy dead.
verses.modern: 'Hear us, my lord; you are a prince of God among us. Bury your dead in the choicest of our tombs. None of us will withhold from you His tomb for burying your dead.'

verses.kjv: And Abraham stood up, and bowed himself to the people of the land, even to the children of Heth.
verses.modern: Abraham rose and bowed to the people of the land, to the sons of Heth.

verses.kjv: And he communed with them, saying, If it be your mind that I should bury my dead out of my sight; hear me, and intreat for me to Ephron the son of Zohar,
verses.modern: He spoke with them, saying, 'If it is your will that I should bury my dead out of my sight, hear me and entreat for me Ephron the son of Zohar,

verses.kjv: That he may give me the cave of Machpelah, which he hath, which is in the end of his field; for as much money as it is worth he shall give it me for a possession of a buryingplace amongst you.
verses.modern: that he may give me the cave of Machpelah, which he owns, which is at the end of his field. For the full price let him give it to me in your presence as property for a burying place.'

verses.kjv: And Ephron dwelt among the children of Heth: and Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham in the audience of the children of Heth, even of all that went in at the gate of his city, saying,
verses.modern: Now Ephron was sitting among the sons of Heth, and Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham in the hearing of the sons of Heth, of all who went in at the gate of his city, saying,

verses.kjv: Nay, my lord, hear me: the field give I thee, and the cave that is therein, I give it thee; in the presence of the sons of my people give I it thee: bury thy dead.
verses.modern: 'No, my lord, hear me. The field I give to you, and the cave that is in it I give to you. In the presence of the sons of my people I give it to you; bury your dead.'

verses.kjv: And Abraham bowed down himself before the people of the land.
verses.modern: Then Abraham bowed down before the people of the land.

verses.kjv: And he spake unto Ephron in the audience of the people of the land, saying, But if thou wilt give it, I pray thee, hear me: I will give thee money for the field; take it of me, and I will bury my dead there.
verses.modern: he spoke to Ephron in the hearing of the people of the land, saying, 'But if you will, please hear me. I will give the price of the field; accept it from me. I will bury my dead there.'

verses.kjv: And Ephron answered Abraham, saying unto him,
verses.modern: Ephron answered Abraham, saying to him,

verses.kjv: My lord, hearken unto me: the land is worth four hundred shekels of silver; what is that betwixt me and thee? bury therefore thy dead.
verses.modern: 'My lord, listen to me. A piece of land worth 400 shekels of silver—what is that between me and you? Bury your dead.'

verses.kjv: And Abraham hearkened unto Ephron; and Abraham weighed to Ephron the silver, which he had named in the audience of the sons of Heth, four hundred shekels of silver, current money with the merchant.
verses.modern: Abraham listened to Ephron, and Abraham weighed out for Ephron the silver that he had named in the hearing of the sons of Heth: 400 shekels of silver, according to the weights current among the merchants.

verses.kjv: And the field of Ephron, which was in Machpelah, which was before Mamre, the field, and the cave which was therein, and all the trees that were in the field, that were in all the borders round about, were made sure
verses.modern: So the field of Ephron in Machpelah, which was facing Mamre, the field with the cave that was in it and all the trees that were in the field, throughout its whole area, was made over

verses.kjv: Unto Abraham for a possession in the presence of the children of Heth, before all that went in at the gate of his city.
verses.modern: to Abraham as a possession in the presence of the sons of Heth, before all who went in at the gate of his city.

verses.kjv: And after this, Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre: the same is Hebron in the land of Canaan.
verses.modern: After this, Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah facing Mamre (that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan.

verses.kjv: And the field, and the cave that is therein, were made sure unto Abraham for a possession of a buryingplace by the sons of Heth.
verses.modern: The field and the cave that was in it were made over to Abraham as property for a burying place by the sons of Heth.

chapters.summary: Sarah died at the age of 127 in Hebron, and Abraham mourned for her. He negotiated with the sons of Heth and purchased the cave of Machpelah and its surrounding field from Ephron the Hittite for 400 shekels of silver. Abraham buried Sarah there — his first piece of land in Canaan.

verses.kjv: And Abraham was old, and well stricken in age: and the LORD had blessed Abraham in all things.
verses.modern: Now Abraham was old, advanced in years. The LORD had blessed Abraham in all things.

verses.kjv: And Abraham said unto his eldest servant of his house, that ruled over all that he had, Put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh:
verses.modern: Abraham said to his oldest servant of his house, who had charge of all he had, 'Put your hand under my thigh,

verses.kjv: And I will make thee swear by the LORD, the God of heaven, and the God of the earth, that thou shalt not take a wife unto my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I dwell:
verses.modern: I will make You swear by the LORD, the God of heaven and the God of the earth, that You will not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I dwell,

verses.kjv: But thou shalt go unto my country, and to my kindred, and take a wife unto my son Isaac.
verses.modern: but will go to my country and to my family and take a wife for my son Isaac.'

verses.kjv: And the servant said unto him, Peradventure the woman will not be willing to follow me unto this land: must I needs bring thy son again unto the land from whence thou camest?
verses.modern: The servant said to him, 'Perhaps the woman will not be willing to follow me to this land. Must I then take your son back to the land from which you came?'

verses.kjv: And Abraham said unto him, Beware thou that thou bring not my son thither again.
verses.modern: Abraham said to him, 'See to it that you do not take my son back there.

verses.kjv: The LORD God of heaven, which took me from my father's house, and from the land of my kindred, and which spake unto me, and that sware unto me, saying, Unto thy seed will I give this land; he shall send his angel before thee, and thou shalt take a wife unto my son from thence.
verses.modern: The LORD, the God of heaven, who took me from my father's house and from the land of my family, and who spoke to me and swore to me, saying, To Your seed I will give this land—He will send His angel before You, and You shall take a wife for my son from there.

verses.kjv: And if the woman will not be willing to follow thee, then thou shalt be clear from this my oath: only bring not my son thither again.
verses.modern: But if the woman is not willing to follow you, then you will be free from this oath of mine; only do not take my son back there.'

verses.kjv: And the servant put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master, and sware to him concerning that matter.
verses.modern: So the servant put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master and swore to him concerning this matter.

verses.kjv: And the servant took ten camels of the camels of his master, and departed; for all the goods of his master were in his hand: and he arose, and went to Mesopotamia, unto the city of Nahor.
verses.modern: Then the servant took ten of his master's camels and departed, taking all sorts of choice gifts from his master. He arose and went to Mesopotamia, to the city of Nahor.

verses.kjv: And he made his camels to kneel down without the city by a well of water at the time of the evening, even the time that women go out to draw water.
verses.modern: he made the camels kneel down outside the city by the well of water at the time of evening, the time when women go out to draw water.

verses.kjv: And he said, O LORD God of my master Abraham, I pray thee, send me good speed this day, and shew kindness unto my master Abraham.
verses.modern: He said, 'O LORD, God of my master Abraham, please grant me success today and show mercy to my master Abraham.

verses.kjv: Behold, I stand here by the well of water; and the daughters of the men of the city come out to draw water:
verses.modern: I stand here by the spring of water, and the daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water.

verses.kjv: And let it come to pass, that the damsel to whom I shall say, Let down thy pitcher, I pray thee, that I may drink; and she shall say, Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also: let the same be she that thou hast appointed for thy servant Isaac; and thereby shall I know that thou hast shewed kindness unto my master.
verses.modern: Let it be that the young woman to whom I shall say, Please let down your jar that I may drink, and who shall say, Drink. I will water your camels also—let her be the one you have appointed for your servant Isaac. By this I shall know that you have shown mercy to my master.'

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, before he had done speaking, that, behold, Rebekah came out, who was born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother, with her pitcher upon her shoulder.
verses.modern: Before he had finished speaking, Rebekah came out, who was born to Bethuel the son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother, with her water jar on her shoulder.

verses.kjv: And the damsel was very fair to look upon, a virgin, neither had any man known her: and she went down to the well, and filled her pitcher, and came up.
verses.modern: The young woman was very beautiful to look at, a virgin; no man had known her. She went down to the spring, filled her jar, and came up.

verses.kjv: And the servant ran to meet her, and said, Let me, I pray thee, drink a little water of thy pitcher.
verses.modern: Then the servant ran to meet her and said, 'Please give me a little water to drink from your jar.'

verses.kjv: And she said, Drink, my lord: and she hasted, and let down her pitcher upon her hand, and gave him drink.
verses.modern: She said, 'Drink, my lord.' And she quickly let down her jar upon her hand and gave him a drink.

verses.kjv: And when she had done giving him drink, she said, I will draw water for thy camels also, until they have done drinking.
verses.modern: When she had finished giving him a drink, she said, 'I will draw water for your camels also, until they have finished drinking.'

verses.kjv: And she hasted, and emptied her pitcher into the trough, and ran again unto the well to draw water, and drew for all his camels.
verses.modern: So she quickly emptied her jar into the trough and ran again to the well to draw water. She drew for all his camels.

verses.kjv: And the man wondering at her held his peace, to wit whether the LORD had made his journey prosperous or not.
verses.modern: The man gazed at her in silence to learn whether the LORD had prospered His journey or not.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, as the camels had done drinking, that the man took a golden earring of half a shekel weight, and two bracelets for her hands of ten shekels weight of gold;
verses.modern: When the camels had finished drinking, the man took a gold ring weighing a half shekel, and two bracelets for her arms weighing ten gold shekels,

verses.kjv: And said, Whose daughter art thou? tell me, I pray thee: is there room in thy father's house for us to lodge in?
verses.modern: He He said, 'Whose daughter are you? Please tell me. Is there room in your father's house for us to spend the night?'

verses.kjv: And she said unto him, I am the daughter of Bethuel the son of Milcah, which she bare unto Nahor.
verses.modern: She said to him, 'I am the daughter of Bethuel the son of Milcah, whom she bore to Nahor.'

verses.kjv: She said moreover unto him, We have both straw and provender enough, and room to lodge in.
verses.modern: She added, 'We have plenty of both straw and fodder, and room to spend the night.'

verses.kjv: And the man bowed down his head, and worshipped the LORD.
verses.modern: The man bowed his head and worshiped the LORD,

verses.kjv: And he said, Blessed be the LORD God of my master Abraham, who hath not left destitute my master of his mercy and his truth: I being in the way, the LORD led me to the house of my master's brethren.
verses.modern: He said, 'Blessed be the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who has not forsaken his mercy and truth toward my master. As for me, the LORD has led me in the way to the house of my master's kinsmen.'

verses.kjv: And the damsel ran, and told them of her mother's house these things.
verses.modern: Then the young woman ran and told her mother's household about these things.

verses.kjv: And Rebekah had a brother, and his name was Laban: and Laban ran out unto the man, unto the well.
verses.modern: Rebekah had a brother whose name was Laban. Laban ran out to the man, to the spring.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, when he saw the earring and bracelets upon his sister's hands, and when he heard the words of Rebekah his sister, saying, Thus spake the man unto me; that he came unto the man; and, behold, he stood by the camels at the well.
verses.modern: As soon as he saw the ring and the bracelets on his sister's arms, and heard the words of Rebekah his sister, 'Thus the man spoke to me,' he went to the man. And he was standing by the camels at the spring.

verses.kjv: And he said, Come in, thou blessed of the LORD; wherefore standest thou without? for I have prepared the house, and room for the camels.
verses.modern: He said, 'Come in, O blessed of the LORD. Why do You stand outside? For I have prepared the house and a place for the camels.'

verses.kjv: And the man came into the house: and he ungirded his camels, and gave straw and provender for the camels, and water to wash his feet, and the men's feet that were with him.
verses.modern: So the man came into the house. He unloaded the camels, and gave straw and fodder to the camels, and there was water to wash his feet and the feet of the men who were with him.

verses.kjv: And there was set meat before him to eat: but he said, I will not eat, until I have told mine errand. And he said, Speak on.
verses.modern: Then food was set before him to eat. But He said, 'I will not eat until I have told my errand.' He said, 'Speak on.'

verses.kjv: And he said, I am Abraham's servant.
verses.modern: So he said, 'I am Abraham's servant.

verses.kjv: And the LORD hath blessed my master greatly; and he is become great: and he hath given him flocks, and herds, and silver, and gold, and menservants, and maidservants, and camels, and asses.
verses.modern: The LORD has greatly blessed my master. He has become great. He has given him flocks and herds, silver and gold, male and female servants, camels and donkeys.

verses.kjv: And Sarah my master's wife bare a son to my master when she was old: and unto him hath he given all that he hath.
verses.modern: Sarah my master's wife bore a son to my master when she was old, and to him he has given all that he has.

verses.kjv: And my master made me swear, saying, Thou shalt not take a wife to my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I dwell:
verses.modern: My master made me swear, saying, You shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I dwell,

verses.kjv: But thou shalt go unto my father's house, and to my kindred, and take a wife unto my son.
verses.modern: but you shall go to my father's house and to my family and take a wife for my son.

verses.kjv: And I said unto my master, Peradventure the woman will not follow me.
verses.modern: I said to my master, Perhaps the woman will not follow me.

verses.kjv: And he said unto me, The LORD, before whom I walk, will send his angel with thee, and prosper thy way; and thou shalt take a wife for my son of my kindred, and of my father's house:
verses.modern: But He said to me, The LORD, before whom I walk, will send His angel with You and prosper Your way. You shall take a wife for my son from my family, from my father's house.

verses.kjv: Then shalt thou be clear from this my oath, when thou comest to my kindred; and if they give not thee one, thou shalt be clear from my oath.
verses.modern: Then You will be free from my oath, when You come to my family. And if they will not give her to You, You will be free from my oath.

verses.kjv: And I came this day unto the well, and said, O LORD God of my master Abraham, if now thou do prosper my way which I go:
verses.modern: I came today to the spring and said, O LORD, God of my master Abraham, if now you are prospering the way that I go,

verses.kjv: Behold, I stand by the well of water; and it shall come to pass, that when the virgin cometh forth to draw water, and I say to her, Give me, I pray thee, a little water of thy pitcher to drink;
verses.modern: I am standing by the spring of water. Let the virgin who comes out to draw water, to whom I shall say, Please give me a little water from Your jar to drink,

verses.kjv: And she say to me, Both drink thou, and I will also draw for thy camels: let the same be the woman whom the LORD hath appointed out for my master's son.
verses.modern: who will say to me, Drink. I will draw for Your camels also—let her be the woman whom the LORD has appointed for my master's son.

verses.kjv: And before I had done speaking in mine heart, behold, Rebekah came forth with her pitcher on her shoulder; and she went down unto the well, and drew water: and I said unto her, Let me drink, I pray thee.
verses.modern: Before I had finished speaking in my heart, Rebekah came out with her water jar on her shoulder. She went down to the spring and drew water. I said to her, Please let me drink.

verses.kjv: And she made haste, and let down her pitcher from her shoulder, and said, Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also: so I drank, and she made the camels drink also.
verses.modern: She quickly let down her jar from her shoulder and said, Drink. I will give your camels drink also. So I drank. She gave the camels drink also.

verses.kjv: And I asked her, and said, Whose daughter art thou? And she said, The daughter of Bethuel, Nahor's son, whom Milcah bare unto him: and I put the earring upon her face, and the bracelets upon her hands.
verses.modern: Then I asked her, Whose daughter are you? She said, The daughter of Bethuel, Nahor's son, whom Milcah bore to him. So I put the ring on her nose and the bracelets on her arms.

verses.kjv: And I bowed down my head, and worshipped the LORD, and blessed the LORD God of my master Abraham, which had led me in the right way to take my master's brother's daughter unto his son.
verses.modern: Then I bowed my head and worshiped the LORD and blessed the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who had led me by the right way to take the daughter of my master's kinsman for His son.

verses.kjv: And now if ye will deal kindly and truly with my master, tell me: and if not, tell me; that I may turn to the right hand, or to the left.
verses.modern: Now then, if You will show mercy and truth to my master, tell me. If not, tell me, that I may turn to the right hand or to the left.'

verses.kjv: Then Laban and Bethuel answered and said, The thing proceedeth from the LORD: we cannot speak unto thee bad or good.
verses.modern: Then Laban and Bethuel answered, 'The thing has come from the LORD; we cannot speak to You bad or good.

verses.kjv: Behold, Rebekah is before thee, take her, and go, and let her be thy master's son's wife, as the LORD hath spoken.
verses.modern: Rebekah is before you; take her and go, and let her be the wife of Your master's son, as the LORD has spoken.'

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that, when Abraham's servant heard their words, he worshipped the LORD, bowing himself to the earth.
verses.modern: When Abraham's servant heard their words, he bowed himself to the earth before the LORD.

verses.kjv: And the servant brought forth jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment, and gave them to Rebekah: he gave also to her brother and to her mother precious things.
verses.modern: The servant brought out jewelry of silver and of gold, and garments, and gave them to Rebekah. He also gave to her brother and to her mother costly gifts.

verses.kjv: And they did eat and drink, he and the men that were with him, and tarried all night; and they rose up in the morning, and he said, Send me away unto my master.
verses.modern: he and the men who were with him ate and drank. They spent the night there. When they arose in the morning, he said, 'Send me away to my master.'

verses.kjv: And her brother and her mother said, Let the damsel abide with us a few days, at the least ten; after that she shall go.
verses.modern: Her brother and her mother said, 'Let the young woman remain with us a while, at least ten days; after that she may go.'

verses.kjv: And he said unto them, Hinder me not, seeing the LORD hath prospered my way; send me away that I may go to my master.
verses.modern: But He said to them, 'Do not delay me, since the LORD has prospered my way. Send me away that I may go to my master.'

verses.kjv: And they said, We will call the damsel, and enquire at her mouth.
verses.modern: They said, 'Let us call the young woman and ask her.'

verses.kjv: And they called Rebekah, and said unto her, Wilt thou go with this man? And she said, I will go.
verses.modern: They called Rebekah and said to her, 'Will you go with this man?' She said, 'I will go.'

verses.kjv: And they sent away Rebekah their sister, and her nurse, and Abraham's servant, and his men.
verses.modern: So they sent away Rebekah their sister and her nurse, and Abraham's servant and his men.

verses.kjv: And they blessed Rebekah, and said unto her, Thou art our sister, be thou the mother of thousands of millions, and let thy seed possess the gate of those which hate them.
verses.modern: They blessed Rebekah and said to her, 'Our sister, may you become the mother of thousands of ten thousands, and may your seed possess the gate of those who hate them.'

verses.kjv: And Rebekah arose, and her damsels, and they rode upon the camels, and followed the man: and the servant took Rebekah, and went his way.
verses.modern: Then Rebekah and her maidservants arose and rode on the camels and followed the man. So the servant took Rebekah and went his way.

verses.kjv: And Isaac came from the way of the well Lahairoi; for he dwelt in the south country.
verses.modern: Now Isaac had returned from Beer-lahai-roi, and was dwelling in the south.

verses.kjv: And Isaac went out to meditate in the field at the eventide: and he lifted up his eyes, and saw, and, behold, the camels were coming.
verses.modern: Isaac went out to meditate in the field toward evening. He lifted up his eyes and saw, and camels were coming.

verses.kjv: And Rebekah lifted up her eyes, and when she saw Isaac, she lighted off the camel.
verses.modern: Rebekah lifted up her eyes, and when she saw Isaac, she dismounted from the camel

verses.kjv: For she had said unto the servant, What man is this that walketh in the field to meet us? And the servant had said, It is my master: therefore she took a vail, and covered herself.
verses.modern: said to the servant, 'Who is that man walking in the field to meet us?' The servant said, 'It is my master.' So she took her veil and covered herself.

verses.kjv: And the servant told Isaac all things that he had done.
verses.modern: The servant told Isaac all the things that he had done.

verses.kjv: And Isaac brought her into his mother Sarah's tent, and took Rebekah, and she became his wife; and he loved her: and Isaac was comforted after his mother's death.
verses.modern: Then Isaac brought her into the tent of Sarah his mother and took Rebekah. She became his wife. He loved her. So Isaac was comforted after his mother's death.

chapters.summary: Abraham sent his servant to Mesopotamia to find a wife for Isaac from among his kinsmen, not from the Canaanites. The servant prayed at the well and God guided him to Rebekah, who watered his camels; her family agreed to the match. Rebekah returned to Canaan and became Isaac's wife, and he loved her.

verses.kjv: Then again Abraham took a wife, and her name was Keturah.
verses.modern: Abraham again took a wife. Her name was Keturah.

verses.kjv: And she bare him Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah.
verses.modern: She bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.

verses.kjv: And Jokshan begat Sheba, and Dedan. And the sons of Dedan were Asshurim, and Letushim, and Leummim.
verses.modern: Jokshan begat Sheba and Dedan. The sons of Dedan were Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim.

verses.kjv: And the sons of Midian; Ephah, and Epher, and Hanoch, and Abidah, and Eldaah. All these were the children of Keturah.
verses.modern: The sons of Midian were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were the children of Keturah.

verses.kjv: And Abraham gave all that he had unto Isaac.
verses.modern: Abraham gave all that he had to Isaac.

verses.kjv: But unto the sons of the concubines, which Abraham had, Abraham gave gifts, and sent them away from Isaac his son, while he yet lived, eastward, unto the east country.
verses.modern: But to the sons of his concubines Abraham gave gifts, and while he was still living he sent them away from his son Isaac, eastward to the east country.

verses.kjv: And these are the days of the years of Abraham's life which he lived, an hundred threescore and fifteen years.
verses.modern: These are the days of the years of Abraham's life, 175 years.

verses.kjv: Then Abraham gave up the ghost, and died in a good old age, an old man, and full of years; and was gathered to his people.
verses.modern: Abraham breathed his last and died in a good old age, an old man full of years, and was gathered to his people.

verses.kjv: And his sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron the son of Zohar the Hittite, which is before Mamre;
verses.modern: Isaac and Ishmael his sons buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron the son of Zohar the Hittite, facing Mamre,

verses.kjv: The field which Abraham purchased of the sons of Heth: there was Abraham buried, and Sarah his wife.
verses.modern: The field that Abraham purchased from the sons of Heth. There Abraham was buried, with Sarah his wife.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass after the death of Abraham, that God blessed his son Isaac; and Isaac dwelt by the well Lahairoi.
verses.modern: After the death of Abraham, God blessed Isaac his son, and Isaac lived at Beer-lahai-roi.

verses.kjv: Now these are the generations of Ishmael, Abraham's son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah's handmaid, bare unto Abraham:
verses.modern: These are the generations of Ishmael, Abraham's son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah's maidservant, bore to Abraham.

verses.kjv: And these are the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names, according to their generations: the firstborn of Ishmael, Nebajoth; and Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam,
verses.modern: These are the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names, according to their generations: the firstborn of Ishmael, Nebajoth, then Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,

verses.kjv: And Mishma, and Dumah, and Massa,
verses.modern: Mishma, Dumah, Massa,

verses.kjv: Hadar, and Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah:
verses.modern: Hadar, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.

verses.kjv: These are the sons of Ishmael, and these are their names, by their towns, and by their castles; twelve princes according to their nations.
verses.modern: These are the sons of Ishmael, and these are their names, by their villages and by their encampments, twelve princes according to their tribes.

verses.kjv: And these are the years of the life of Ishmael, an hundred and thirty and seven years: and he gave up the ghost and died; and was gathered unto his people.
verses.modern: These are the years of the life of Ishmael: 137 years. He breathed his last and died, and was gathered to his people.

verses.kjv: And they dwelt from Havilah unto Shur, that is before Egypt, as thou goest toward Assyria: and he died in the presence of all his brethren.
verses.modern: They settled from Havilah to Shur, which is opposite Egypt in the direction of Assyria. He settled over against all his kinsmen.

verses.kjv: And these are the generations of Isaac, Abraham's son: Abraham begat Isaac:
verses.modern: These are the generations of Isaac, Abraham's son: Abraham begat Isaac,

verses.kjv: And Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah to wife, the daughter of Bethuel the Syrian of Padanaram, the sister to Laban the Syrian.
verses.modern: Isaac was 40 years old when he took Rebekah to be his wife, the daughter of Bethuel the Syrian of Padanaram, the sister of Laban the Syrian.

verses.kjv: And Isaac intreated the LORD for his wife, because she was barren: and the LORD was intreated of him, and Rebekah his wife conceived.
verses.modern: Isaac prayed to the LORD for his wife, because she was barren. And the LORD granted His prayer, and Rebekah his wife conceived.

verses.kjv: And the children struggled together within her; and she said, If it be so, why am I thus? And she went to enquire of the LORD.
verses.modern: The children struggled together within her. She said, 'If it is thus, why is this happening to me?' So she went to inquire of the LORD.

verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto her, Two nations are in thy womb, and two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels; and the one people shall be stronger than the other people; and the elder shall serve the younger.
verses.modern: The LORD said to her, 'Two nations are in Your womb, and two peoples from within You shall be divided; the one shall be stronger than the other, the older shall serve the younger.'

verses.kjv: And when her days to be delivered were fulfilled, behold, there were twins in her womb.
verses.modern: When her days to be delivered were fulfilled, there were twins in her womb.

verses.kjv: And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau.
verses.modern: The first came out red, all his body like a hairy cloak, so they called his name Esau.

verses.kjv: And after that came his brother out, and his hand took hold on Esau's heel; and his name was called Jacob: and Isaac was threescore years old when she bare them.
verses.modern: Afterward his brother came out with his hand holding Esau's heel, so his name was called Jacob. Isaac was 60 years old when she bore them.

verses.kjv: And the boys grew: and Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field; and Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents.
verses.modern: The boys grew up. Esau was a skillful hunter, a man of the field, while Jacob was a quiet man, dwelling in tents.

verses.kjv: And Isaac loved Esau, because he did eat of his venison: but Rebekah loved Jacob.
verses.modern: Isaac loved Esau because he ate of his game, but Rebekah loved Jacob.

verses.kjv: And Jacob sod pottage: and Esau came from the field, and he was faint:
verses.modern: Once when Jacob was cooking stew, Esau came in from the field. He was exhausted.

verses.kjv: And Esau said to Jacob, Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage; for I am faint: therefore was his name called Edom.
verses.modern: Esau said to Jacob, 'Let me have some of that red stew, for I am exhausted.' Therefore his name was called Edom.

verses.kjv: And Jacob said, Sell me this day thy birthright.
verses.modern: Jacob said, 'Sell me your birthright first.'

verses.kjv: And Esau said, Behold, I am at the point to die: and what profit shall this birthright do to me?
verses.modern: Esau said, ' I am about to die; of what use is a birthright to me?'

verses.kjv: And Jacob said, Swear to me this day; and he sware unto him: and he sold his birthright unto Jacob.
verses.modern: Jacob said, 'Swear to me first.' So he swore to him and sold his birthright to Jacob.

verses.kjv: Then Jacob gave Esau bread and pottage of lentiles; and he did eat and drink, and rose up, and went his way: thus Esau despised his birthright.
verses.modern: Then Jacob gave Esau bread and lentil stew. He ate and drank and rose and went his way. Thus Esau despised his birthright.

chapters.summary: Abraham married Keturah and had six more sons, but gave all he owned to Isaac; Abraham died at 175 and was buried at Machpelah. Ishmael's twelve sons are listed, and Ishmael died at 137. Rebekah conceived twins — Esau and Jacob; Esau sold his birthright to Jacob for a bowl of lentil stew.

verses.kjv: And there was a famine in the land, beside the first famine that was in the days of Abraham. And Isaac went unto Abimelech king of the Philistines unto Gerar.
verses.modern: There was a famine in the land, besides the former famine that was in the days of Abraham. And Isaac went to Abimelech king of the Philistines in Gerar.

verses.kjv: And the LORD appeared unto him, and said, Go not down into Egypt; dwell in the land which I shall tell thee of:
verses.modern: The LORD appeared to Him and said, 'Do not go down to Egypt; dwell in the land of which I shall tell You.

verses.kjv: Sojourn in this land, and I will be with thee, and will bless thee; for unto thee, and unto thy seed, I will give all these countries, and I will perform the oath which I sware unto Abraham thy father;
verses.modern: stay in this land. I will be with you and will bless you, for to you and to your seed I will give all these lands. I will establish the oath that I swore to Abraham your father.

verses.kjv: And I will make thy seed to multiply as the stars of heaven, and will give unto thy seed all these countries; and in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed;
verses.modern: I will multiply your seed as the stars of the heavens and will give to your seed all these lands. And in your seed all the nations of the earth shall be blessed,

verses.kjv: Because that Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.
verses.modern: because Abraham obeyed my voice and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.'

verses.kjv: And Isaac dwelt in Gerar:
verses.modern: So Isaac lived in Gerar.

verses.kjv: And the men of the place asked him of his wife; and he said, She is my sister: for he feared to say, She is my wife; lest, said he, the men of the place should kill me for Rebekah; because she was fair to look upon.
verses.modern: When the men of the place asked him about his wife, he said, 'She is my sister,' for he feared to say, 'She is my wife,' thinking, 'The men of the place might kill me because of Rebekah, for she is beautiful to look at.'

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, when he had been there a long time, that Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out at a window, and saw, and, behold, Isaac was sporting with Rebekah his wife.
verses.modern: When he had been there a long time, Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out of a window and saw Isaac caressing Rebekah his wife.

verses.kjv: And Abimelech called Isaac, and said, Behold, of a surety she is thy wife: and how saidst thou, She is my sister? And Isaac said unto him, Because I said, Lest I die for her.
verses.modern: So Abimelech called Isaac and said, ' she is surely your wife. How then could you say, She is my sister?' Isaac said to him, 'Because I thought, Lest I die because of her.'

verses.kjv: And Abimelech said, What is this thou hast done unto us? one of the people might lightly have lien with thy wife, and thou shouldest have brought guiltiness upon us.
verses.modern: Abimelech said, 'What is this you have done to us? One of the people might easily have lain with your wife, and you would have brought guilt upon us.'

verses.kjv: And Abimelech charged all his people, saying, He that toucheth this man or his wife shall surely be put to death.
verses.modern: So Abimelech commanded all the people, saying, 'Whoever touches this man or his wife shall surely be put to death.'

verses.kjv: Then Isaac sowed in that land, and received in the same year an hundredfold: and the LORD blessed him.
verses.modern: Isaac sowed in that land and reaped in the same year a hundredfold. The LORD blessed Him,

verses.kjv: And the man waxed great, and went forward, and grew until he became very great:
verses.modern: The man became rich, and gained more and more until he became very wealthy.

verses.kjv: For he had possession of flocks, and possession of herds, and great store of servants: and the Philistines envied him.
verses.modern: He had possessions of flocks and herds and many servants, so that the Philistines envied him.

verses.kjv: For all the wells which his father's servants had digged in the days of Abraham his father, the Philistines had stopped them, and filled them with earth.
verses.modern: Now the Philistines had stopped up and filled with earth all the wells that his father's servants had dug in the days of Abraham his father.

verses.kjv: And Abimelech said unto Isaac, Go from us; for thou art much mightier than we.
verses.modern: Abimelech said to Isaac, 'Go away from us, for you are much mightier than we.'

verses.kjv: And Isaac departed thence, and pitched his tent in the valley of Gerar, and dwelt there.
verses.modern: So Isaac departed from there and pitched his tent in the Valley of Gerar and lived there.

verses.kjv: And Isaac digged again the wells of water, which they had digged in the days of Abraham his father; for the Philistines had stopped them after the death of Abraham: and he called their names after the names by which his father had called them.
verses.modern: Isaac dug again the wells of water that had been dug in the days of Abraham his father, which the Philistines had stopped after the death of Abraham. He gave them the names that his father had called them.

verses.kjv: And Isaac's servants digged in the valley, and found there a well of springing water.
verses.modern: But when Isaac's servants dug in the valley and found there a well of fresh water,

verses.kjv: And the herdmen of Gerar did strive with Isaac's herdmen, saying, The water is ours: and he called the name of the well Esek; because they strove with him.
verses.modern: The herdsmen of Gerar quarreled with Isaac's herdsmen, saying, 'The water is ours.' So he called the name of the well Esek, because they quarreled with him.

verses.kjv: And they digged another well, and strove for that also: and he called the name of it Sitnah.
verses.modern: Then they dug another well. They quarreled over that also, so he called its name Sitnah.

verses.kjv: And he removed from thence, and digged another well; and for that they strove not: and he called the name of it Rehoboth; and he said, For now the LORD hath made room for us, and we shall be fruitful in the land.
verses.modern: He moved from there and dug another well. They did not quarrel over it. So He called its name Rehoboth, saying, 'For now the LORD has made room for us. We shall be fruitful in the land.'

verses.kjv: And he went up from thence to Beersheba.
verses.modern: From there He went up to Beersheba.

verses.kjv: And the LORD appeared unto him the same night, and said, I am the God of Abraham thy father: fear not, for I am with thee, and will bless thee, and multiply thy seed for my servant Abraham's sake.
verses.modern: The LORD appeared to Him the same night and said, 'I am the God of Abraham your father. Do not fear, for I am with you and will bless You and multiply Your seed for my servant Abraham's sake.'

verses.kjv: And he builded an altar there, and called upon the name of the LORD, and pitched his tent there: and there Isaac's servants digged a well.
verses.modern: So He built an altar there and called on the name of the LORD and pitched his tent there, and there Isaac's servants dug a well.

verses.kjv: Then Abimelech went to him from Gerar, and Ahuzzath one of his friends, and Phichol the chief captain of his army.
verses.modern: Then Abimelech went to Him from Gerar with Ahuzzath His friend and Phichol the commander of His army.

verses.kjv: And Isaac said unto them, Wherefore come ye to me, seeing ye hate me, and have sent me away from you?
verses.modern: Isaac said to them, 'Why have you come to me, seeing you hate me and have sent me away from you?'

verses.kjv: And they said, We saw certainly that the LORD was with thee: and we said, Let there be now an oath betwixt us, even betwixt us and thee, and let us make a covenant with thee;
verses.modern: They said, 'We see plainly that the LORD has been with You. So we said, Let there be an oath between us, between You and us, and let us make a covenant with You,

verses.kjv: That thou wilt do us no hurt, as we have not touched thee, and as we have done unto thee nothing but good, and have sent thee away in peace: thou art now the blessed of the LORD.
verses.modern: that You will do us no harm, just as we have not touched You and have done to You nothing but good and have sent You away in peace. You are now the blessed of the LORD.'

verses.kjv: And he made them a feast, and they did eat and drink.
verses.modern: So He made them a feast. They ate and drank.

verses.kjv: And they rose up betimes in the morning, and sware one to another: and Isaac sent them away, and they departed from him in peace.
verses.modern: In the morning they rose early and exchanged oaths. Then Isaac sent them on their way. They departed from him in peace.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass the same day, that Isaac's servants came, and told him concerning the well which they had digged, and said unto him, We have found water.
verses.modern: That same day Isaac's servants came and told him about the well that they had dug, and said to him, 'We have found water.'

verses.kjv: And he called it Shebah: therefore the name of the city is Beersheba unto this day.
verses.modern: He called it Shebah; therefore the name of the city is Beersheba to this day.

verses.kjv: And Esau was forty years old when he took to wife Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Bashemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite:
verses.modern: When Esau was 40 years old, he took Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite as his wife, and Bashemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite.

verses.kjv: Which were a grief of mind unto Isaac and to Rebekah.
verses.modern: They made life bitter for Isaac and Rebekah.

chapters.summary: A famine drove Isaac to Gerar, where the LORD appeared and confirmed the covenant promises made to Abraham. Isaac told the men of Gerar that Rebekah was his sister, but Abimelech discovered the deception; nonetheless Isaac prospered greatly and dug wells that the Philistines disputed. Abimelech sought a covenant of peace with Isaac at Beersheba, and Esau married Hittite wives who grieved his parents.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that when Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim, so that he could not see, he called Esau his eldest son, and said unto him, My son: and he said unto him, Behold, here am I.
verses.modern: When Isaac was old and his eyes were dim so that he could not see, he called Esau his older son and said to him, 'My son.' And he said to him, 'Here I am.'

verses.kjv: And he said, Behold now, I am old, I know not the day of my death:
verses.modern: He said, ' I am now old; I do not know the day of my death.

verses.kjv: Now therefore take, I pray thee, thy weapons, thy quiver and thy bow, and go out to the field, and take me some venison;
verses.modern: Now then, take your weapons, your quiver and your bow, and go out to the field and hunt game for me.

verses.kjv: And make me savoury meat, such as I love, and bring it to me, that I may eat; that my soul may bless thee before I die.
verses.modern: prepare for me savory food, such as I love, and bring it to me so that I may eat, that my soul may bless you before I die.'

verses.kjv: And Rebekah heard when Isaac spake to Esau his son. And Esau went to the field to hunt for venison, and to bring it.
verses.modern: Rebekah was listening when Isaac spoke to his son Esau. So when Esau went to the field to hunt for game and bring it,

verses.kjv: And Rebekah spake unto Jacob her son, saying, Behold, I heard thy father speak unto Esau thy brother, saying,
verses.modern: Rebekah said to her son Jacob, ' I heard your father speak to your brother Esau, saying,

verses.kjv: Bring me venison, and make me savoury meat, that I may eat, and bless thee before the LORD before my death.
verses.modern: Bring me game and prepare for me savory food, that I may eat it and bless You before the LORD before my death.

verses.kjv: Now therefore, my son, obey my voice according to that which I command thee.
verses.modern: Now therefore, my son, obey my voice in what I command You.

verses.kjv: Go now to the flock, and fetch me from thence two good kids of the goats; and I will make them savoury meat for thy father, such as he loveth:
verses.modern: Go to the flock and bring me from there two good young goats, so that I may prepare from them savory food for Your father, such as He loves.

verses.kjv: And thou shalt bring it to thy father, that he may eat, and that he may bless thee before his death.
verses.modern: you shall bring it to Your father to eat, that He may bless You before His death.'

verses.kjv: And Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, Behold, Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man:
verses.modern: But Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, ' my brother Esau is a hairy man. I am a smooth man.

verses.kjv: My father peradventure will feel me, and I shall seem to him as a deceiver; and I shall bring a curse upon me, and not a blessing.
verses.modern: Perhaps my father will feel me. I shall seem to him as a deceiver and bring a curse upon myself and not a blessing.'

verses.kjv: And his mother said unto him, Upon me be thy curse, my son: only obey my voice, and go fetch me them.
verses.modern: His mother said to him, 'Upon me be your curse, my son; only obey my voice and go, bring them to me.'

verses.kjv: And he went, and fetched, and brought them to his mother: and his mother made savoury meat, such as his father loved.
verses.modern: So he went and took them and brought them to his mother. His mother prepared savory food, such as his father loved.

verses.kjv: And Rebekah took goodly raiment of her eldest son Esau, which were with her in the house, and put them upon Jacob her younger son:
verses.modern: Then Rebekah took the best garments of Esau her older son, which were with her in the house, and put them on Jacob her younger son.

verses.kjv: And she put the skins of the kids of the goats upon his hands, and upon the smooth of his neck:
verses.modern: she put the skins of the young goats on his hands and on the smooth part of his neck.

verses.kjv: And she gave the savoury meat and the bread, which she had prepared, into the hand of her son Jacob.
verses.modern: Then she put the savory food and the bread which she had prepared into the hand of her son Jacob.

verses.kjv: And he came unto his father, and said, My father: and he said, Here am I; who art thou, my son?
verses.modern: So he went to his father and said, 'My father.' And he said, 'Here I am. Who are you, my son?'

verses.kjv: And Jacob said unto his father, I am Esau thy firstborn; I have done according as thou badest me: arise, I pray thee, sit and eat of my venison, that thy soul may bless me.
verses.modern: Jacob said to his father, 'I am Esau your firstborn. I have done as you told me. Please arise, sit and eat of my game, that your soul may bless me.'

verses.kjv: And Isaac said unto his son, How is it that thou hast found it so quickly, my son? And he said, Because the LORD thy God brought it to me.
verses.modern: Isaac said to his son, 'How is it that you have found it so quickly, my son?' He said, 'Because the LORD Your God granted me success.'

verses.kjv: And Isaac said unto Jacob, Come near, I pray thee, that I may feel thee, my son, whether thou be my very son Esau or not.
verses.modern: Then Isaac said to Jacob, 'Please come near, that I may feel you, my son, to know whether you are really my son Esau or not.'

verses.kjv: And Jacob went near unto Isaac his father; and he felt him, and said, The voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.
verses.modern: So Jacob went near to Isaac his father, who felt him and said, 'The voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.'

verses.kjv: And he discerned him not, because his hands were hairy, as his brother Esau's hands: so he blessed him.
verses.modern: He did not recognize him, because his hands were hairy like his brother Esau's hands. So he blessed him.

verses.kjv: And he said, Art thou my very son Esau? And he said, I am.
verses.modern: He said, 'Are you really my son Esau?' He answered, 'I am.'

verses.kjv: And he said, Bring it near to me, and I will eat of my son's venison, that my soul may bless thee. And he brought it near to him, and he did eat: and he brought him wine, and he drank.
verses.modern: Then he said, 'Bring it near to me, that I may eat of my son's game and my soul may bless you.' So he brought it near to him. He ate. He brought him wine. He drank.

verses.kjv: And his father Isaac said unto him, Come near now, and kiss me, my son.
verses.modern: Then his father Isaac said to him, 'Come near and kiss me, my son.'

verses.kjv: And he came near, and kissed him: and he smelled the smell of his raiment, and blessed him, and said, See, the smell of my son is as the smell of a field which the LORD hath blessed:
verses.modern: So He came near and kissed Him. And He smelled the smell of His garments and blessed Him, and said, 'See, the smell of my son is like the smell of a field that the LORD has blessed.

verses.kjv: Therefore God give thee of the dew of heaven, and the fatness of the earth, and plenty of corn and wine:
verses.modern: May God give You of the dew of heaven and of the fatness of the earth, and plenty of grain and wine.

verses.kjv: Let people serve thee, and nations bow down to thee: be lord over thy brethren, and let thy mother's sons bow down to thee: cursed be every one that curseth thee, and blessed be he that blesseth thee.
verses.modern: Let peoples serve You, and nations bow down to You. Be lord over Your brothers, and may Your mother's sons bow down to You. Cursed be everyone who curses You, and blessed be everyone who blesses You.'

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, as soon as Isaac had made an end of blessing Jacob, and Jacob was yet scarce gone out from the presence of Isaac his father, that Esau his brother came in from his hunting.
verses.modern: As soon as Isaac had finished blessing Jacob, when Jacob had scarcely gone out from the presence of Isaac his father, Esau his brother came in from his hunting.

verses.kjv: And he also had made savoury meat, and brought it unto his father, and said unto his father, Let my father arise, and eat of his son's venison, that thy soul may bless me.
verses.modern: He also prepared savory food and brought it to his father. And he said to his father, 'Let my father arise and eat of his son's game, that your soul may bless me.'

verses.kjv: And Isaac his father said unto him, Who art thou? And he said, I am thy son, thy firstborn Esau.
verses.modern: His father Isaac said to him, 'Who are you?' He answered, 'I am your son, your firstborn, Esau.'

verses.kjv: And Isaac trembled very exceedingly, and said, Who? where is he that hath taken venison, and brought it me, and I have eaten of all before thou camest, and have blessed him? yea, and he shall be blessed.
verses.modern: Then Isaac trembled violently and said, 'Who then was it that hunted game and brought it to me, so that I ate of it all before you came, and have blessed him? Yes, and he shall be blessed.'

verses.kjv: And when Esau heard the words of his father, he cried with a great and exceeding bitter cry, and said unto his father, Bless me, even me also, O my father.
verses.modern: When Esau heard the words of his father, he cried out with an exceedingly great and bitter cry and said to his father, 'Bless me, even me also, O my father!'

verses.kjv: And he said, Thy brother came with subtilty, and hath taken away thy blessing.
verses.modern: But he said, 'Your brother came with deceit and has taken away your blessing.'

verses.kjv: And he said, Is not he rightly named Jacob? for he hath supplanted me these two times: he took away my birthright; and, behold, now he hath taken away my blessing. And he said, Hast thou not reserved a blessing for me?
verses.modern: Esau said, 'Is he not rightly named Jacob? For he has supplanted me these two times. He took away my birthright, and now he has taken away my blessing.' Then he said, 'Have you not reserved a blessing for me?'

verses.kjv: And Isaac answered and said unto Esau, Behold, I have made him thy lord, and all his brethren have I given to him for servants; and with corn and wine have I sustained him: and what shall I do now unto thee, my son?
verses.modern: Isaac answered and said to Esau, ' I have made him lord over you. All his brothers I have given him for servants, and with grain and wine I have sustained him. What then can I do for you, my son?'

verses.kjv: And Esau said unto his father, Hast thou but one blessing, my father? bless me, even me also, O my father. And Esau lifted up his voice, and wept.
verses.modern: Esau said to his father, 'Have you but one blessing, my father? Bless me, even me also, O my father.' And Esau lifted up his voice and wept.

verses.kjv: And Isaac his father answered and said unto him, Behold, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above;
verses.modern: Then Isaac his father answered and said to him, 'Your dwelling shall be of the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above.

verses.kjv: And by thy sword shalt thou live, and shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck.
verses.modern: By your sword you shall live, and you shall serve your brother. But when you have the dominion, you shall break his yoke from off your neck.'

verses.kjv: And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.
verses.modern: Now Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing with which his father had blessed him. And Esau said in his heart, 'The days of mourning for my father are near; then I will kill my brother Jacob.'

verses.kjv: And these words of Esau her elder son were told to Rebekah: and she sent and called Jacob her younger son, and said unto him, Behold, thy brother Esau, as touching thee, doth comfort himself, purposing to kill thee.
verses.modern: But the words of Esau her older son were told to Rebekah. So she sent and called Jacob her younger son and said to him, ' your brother Esau is comforting himself concerning you by planning to kill you.

verses.kjv: Now therefore, my son, obey my voice; and arise, flee thou to Laban my brother to Haran;
verses.modern: Now therefore, my son, obey my voice. Arise, flee to Laban my brother in Haran,

verses.kjv: And tarry with him a few days, until thy brother's fury turn away;
verses.modern: stay with him a few days, until your brother's fury turns away,

verses.kjv: Until thy brother's anger turn away from thee, and he forget that which thou hast done to him: then I will send, and fetch thee from thence: why should I be deprived also of you both in one day?
verses.modern: until your brother's anger turns away from you and he forgets what you have done to him. Then I will send and bring you from there. Why should I be bereaved of you both in one day?'

verses.kjv: And Rebekah said to Isaac, I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth: if Jacob take a wife of the daughters of Heth, such as these which are of the daughters of the land, what good shall my life do me?
verses.modern: Then Rebekah said to Isaac, 'I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth. If Jacob takes a wife of the daughters of Heth, like these, from the daughters of the land, what good shall my life be to me?'

chapters.summary: Isaac, old and blind, sent Esau to hunt game so he could bless him, but Rebekah and Jacob deceived Isaac with goat skins and savory food, and Jacob received the firstborn's blessing. When Esau returned and the deception was discovered, Isaac trembled and Esau wept bitterly, receiving only a lesser blessing. Esau resolved to kill Jacob, so Rebekah urged Jacob to flee to her brother Laban in Haran.

verses.kjv: And Isaac called Jacob, and blessed him, and charged him, and said unto him, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan.
verses.modern: Then Isaac called Jacob and blessed him and commanded him, 'You shall not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan.

verses.kjv: Arise, go to Padanaram, to the house of Bethuel thy mother's father; and take thee a wife from thence of the daughters of Laban thy mother's brother.
verses.modern: Arise, go to Padanaram to the house of Bethuel your mother's father, and take as your wife from there one of the daughters of Laban your mother's brother.

verses.kjv: And God Almighty bless thee, and make thee fruitful, and multiply thee, that thou mayest be a multitude of people;
verses.modern: God Almighty bless you and make you fruitful and multiply you, that you may become a company of peoples.

verses.kjv: And give thee the blessing of Abraham, to thee, and to thy seed with thee; that thou mayest inherit the land wherein thou art a stranger, which God gave unto Abraham.
verses.modern: May he give the blessing of Abraham to you and to your seed with you, that you may take possession of the land of your sojournings, which God gave to Abraham.'

verses.kjv: And Isaac sent away Jacob: and he went to Padanaram unto Laban, son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebekah, Jacob's and Esau's mother.
verses.modern: So Isaac sent Jacob away. He went to Padanaram, to Laban, the son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebekah, Jacob's and Esau's mother.

verses.kjv: When Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob, and sent him away to Padanaram, to take him a wife from thence; and that as he blessed him he gave him a charge, saying, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan;
verses.modern: Now when Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him away to Padanaram to take a wife from there, and that as he blessed him he commanded him, 'You shall not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan,'

verses.kjv: And that Jacob obeyed his father and his mother, and was gone to Padanaram;
verses.modern: that Jacob had obeyed his father and his mother and had gone to Padanaram,

verses.kjv: And Esau seeing that the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac his father;
verses.modern: Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan did not please Isaac his father.

verses.kjv: Then went Esau unto Ishmael, and took unto the wives which he had Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael Abraham's son, the sister of Nebajoth, to be his wife.
verses.modern: So Esau went to Ishmael and took Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael, Abraham's son, the sister of Nebajoth, in addition to the wives he had, to be his wife.

verses.kjv: And Jacob went out from Beersheba, and went toward Haran.
verses.modern: Jacob left Beersheba and went toward Haran.

verses.kjv: And he lighted upon a certain place, and tarried there all night, because the sun was set; and he took of the stones of that place, and put them for his pillows, and lay down in that place to sleep.
verses.modern: He came to a certain place and stayed there that night, because the sun had set. Taking one of the stones of the place, he put it under his head and lay down in that place to sleep.

verses.kjv: And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven: and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it.
verses.modern: He dreamed, and there was a ladder set up on the earth, and its top reached to heaven. And the angels of God were ascending and descending on it.

verses.kjv: And, behold, the LORD stood above it, and said, I am the LORD God of Abraham thy father, and the God of Isaac: the land whereon thou liest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed;
verses.modern: The LORD stood above it and said, 'I am the LORD, the God of Abraham your father and the God of Isaac. The land on which you lie I will give to you and to Your seed.

verses.kjv: And thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and thou shalt spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south: and in thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed.
verses.modern: Your seed shall be like the dust of the earth, and You shall spread abroad to the west and to the east and to the north and to the south. And in You and in Your seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed.

verses.kjv: And, behold, I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places whither thou goest, and will bring thee again into this land; for I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken to thee of.
verses.modern: I am with You and will keep You wherever You go, and will bring You back to this land. For I will not leave You until I have done what I have promised You.'

verses.kjv: And Jacob awaked out of his sleep, and he said, Surely the LORD is in this place; and I knew it not.
verses.modern: Then Jacob awoke from his sleep and said, 'Surely the LORD is in this place. I did not know it.'

verses.kjv: And he was afraid, and said, How dreadful is this place! this is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.
verses.modern: He was afraid and said, 'How awesome is this place! This is none other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.'

verses.kjv: And Jacob rose up early in the morning, and took the stone that he had put for his pillows, and set it up for a pillar, and poured oil upon the top of it.
verses.modern: So early in the morning Jacob took the stone that he had put under his head and set it up for a pillar and poured oil on the top of it.

verses.kjv: And he called the name of that place Bethel: but the name of that city was called Luz at the first.
verses.modern: He called the name of that place Bethel, but the name of the city was Luz at first.

verses.kjv: And Jacob vowed a vow, saying, If God will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on,
verses.modern: Then Jacob made a vow, saying, 'If God will be with me and will keep me in this way that I go and will give me bread to eat and clothing to wear,

verses.kjv: So that I come again to my father's house in peace; then shall the LORD be my God:
verses.modern: so that I come again to my father's house in peace, then the LORD shall be my God,

verses.kjv: And this stone, which I have set for a pillar, shall be God's house: and of all that thou shalt give me I will surely give the tenth unto thee.
verses.modern: this stone, which I have set up for a pillar, shall be God's house. And of all that You give me I will give a full tenth to You.'

chapters.summary: Isaac blessed Jacob and sent him to Padanaram to take a wife from Laban's daughters; Esau, seeing this, married a daughter of Ishmael. On the way, Jacob slept at a certain place and dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven with angels ascending and descending; the LORD stood above it and renewed the covenant promises. Jacob named the place Bethel and vowed that the LORD would be his God.

verses.kjv: Then Jacob went on his journey, and came into the land of the people of the east.
verses.modern: Then Jacob went on his journey and came to the land of the people of the east.

verses.kjv: And he looked, and behold a well in the field, and, lo, there were three flocks of sheep lying by it; for out of that well they watered the flocks: and a great stone was upon the well's mouth.
verses.modern: As he looked, he saw a well in the field, and three flocks of sheep lying beside it, for from that well they watered the flocks. The stone on the well's mouth was large.

verses.kjv: And thither were all the flocks gathered: and they rolled the stone from the well's mouth, and watered the sheep, and put the stone again upon the well's mouth in his place.
verses.modern: When all the flocks were gathered there, the shepherds would roll the stone from the mouth of the well and water the sheep, and put the stone back in its place on the mouth of the well.

verses.kjv: And Jacob said unto them, My brethren, whence be ye? And they said, Of Haran are we.
verses.modern: Jacob said to them, 'My brothers, where do you come from?' They said, 'We are from Haran.'

verses.kjv: And he said unto them, Know ye Laban the son of Nahor? And they said, We know him.
verses.modern: He said to them, 'Do you know Laban the son of Nahor?' They said, 'We know him.'

verses.kjv: And he said unto them, Is he well? And they said, He is well: and, behold, Rachel his daughter cometh with the sheep.
verses.modern: He said to them, 'Is it well with him?' They said, 'It is well. Rachel his daughter is coming with the sheep.'

verses.kjv: And he said, Lo, it is yet high day, neither is it time that the cattle should be gathered together: water ye the sheep, and go and feed them.
verses.modern: He said, ' it is still high day; it is not time for the livestock to be gathered together. Water the sheep and go, pasture them.'

verses.kjv: And they said, We cannot, until all the flocks be gathered together, and till they roll the stone from the well's mouth; then we water the sheep.
verses.modern: But they said, 'We cannot until all the flocks are gathered together and the stone is rolled from the mouth of the well; then we water the sheep.'

verses.kjv: And while he yet spake with them, Rachel came with her father's sheep: for she kept them.
verses.modern: While he was still speaking with them, Rachel came with her father's sheep, for she kept them.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, when Jacob saw Rachel the daughter of Laban his mother's brother, and the sheep of Laban his mother's brother, that Jacob went near, and rolled the stone from the well's mouth, and watered the flock of Laban his mother's brother.
verses.modern: When Jacob saw Rachel the daughter of Laban his mother's brother and the sheep of Laban his mother's brother, Jacob came near and rolled the stone from the mouth of the well and watered the flock of Laban his mother's brother.

verses.kjv: And Jacob kissed Rachel, and lifted up his voice, and wept.
verses.modern: Then Jacob kissed Rachel and wept aloud.

verses.kjv: And Jacob told Rachel that he was her father's brother, and that he was Rebekah's son: and she ran and told her father.
verses.modern: Jacob told Rachel that he was her father's kinsman and that he was Rebekah's son. She ran and told her father.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, when Laban heard the tidings of Jacob his sister's son, that he ran to meet him, and embraced him, and kissed him, and brought him to his house. And he told Laban all these things.
verses.modern: As soon as Laban heard the news about Jacob his sister's son, he ran to meet him and embraced him and kissed him and brought him to his house. Jacob told Laban all these things,

verses.kjv: And Laban said to him, Surely thou art my bone and my flesh. And he abode with him the space of a month.
verses.modern: Laban said to him, 'Surely you are my bone and my flesh.' And he stayed with him a month.

verses.kjv: And Laban said unto Jacob, Because thou art my brother, shouldest thou therefore serve me for nought? tell me, what shall thy wages be?
verses.modern: Then Laban said to Jacob, 'Because you are my kinsman, should you therefore serve me for nothing? Tell me, what shall your wages be?'

verses.kjv: And Laban had two daughters: the name of the elder was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.
verses.modern: Now Laban had two daughters: the name of the older was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.

verses.kjv: Leah was tender eyed; but Rachel was beautiful and well favoured.
verses.modern: Leah's eyes were weak, but Rachel was beautiful in form and appearance.

verses.kjv: And Jacob loved Rachel; and said, I will serve thee seven years for Rachel thy younger daughter.
verses.modern: Jacob loved Rachel. He said, 'I will serve you seven years for your younger daughter Rachel.'

verses.kjv: And Laban said, It is better that I give her to thee, than that I should give her to another man: abide with me.
verses.modern: Laban said, 'It is better that I give her to you than that I should give her to any other man; stay with me.'

verses.kjv: And Jacob served seven years for Rachel; and they seemed unto him but a few days, for the love he had to her.
verses.modern: So Jacob served seven years for Rachel. They seemed to him but a few days because of the love he had for her.

verses.kjv: And Jacob said unto Laban, Give me my wife, for my days are fulfilled, that I may go in unto her.
verses.modern: Then Jacob said to Laban, 'Give me my wife, for my time is completed, that I may go in to her.'

verses.kjv: And Laban gathered together all the men of the place, and made a feast.
verses.modern: So Laban gathered together all the men of the place and made a feast.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass in the evening, that he took Leah his daughter, and brought her to him; and he went in unto her.
verses.modern: But in the evening he took his daughter Leah and brought her to Jacob. He went in to her.

verses.kjv: And Laban gave unto his daughter Leah Zilpah his maid for an handmaid.
verses.modern: Laban gave his female servant Zilpah to his daughter Leah to be her servant.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that in the morning, behold, it was Leah: and he said to Laban, What is this thou hast done unto me? did not I serve with thee for Rachel? wherefore then hast thou beguiled me?
verses.modern: In the morning, it was Leah! And Jacob said to Laban, 'What is this you have done to me? Did I not serve with you for Rachel? Why then have you deceived me?'

verses.kjv: And Laban said, It must not be so done in our country, to give the younger before the firstborn.
verses.modern: Laban said, 'It is not so done in our country, to give the younger before the firstborn.

verses.kjv: Fulfil her week, and we will give thee this also for the service which thou shalt serve with me yet seven other years.
verses.modern: Complete the week of this one. We will give you the other also in return for serving me another seven years.'

verses.kjv: And Jacob did so, and fulfilled her week: and he gave him Rachel his daughter to wife also.
verses.modern: Jacob did so, and completed her week. Then Laban gave him his daughter Rachel to be his wife.

verses.kjv: And Laban gave to Rachel his daughter Bilhah his handmaid to be her maid.
verses.modern: Laban gave his female servant Bilhah to his daughter Rachel to be her servant.

verses.kjv: And he went in also unto Rachel, and he loved also Rachel more than Leah, and served with him yet seven other years.
verses.modern: So Jacob went in to Rachel also. He loved Rachel more than Leah, and served Laban for another seven years.

verses.kjv: And when the LORD saw that Leah was hated, he opened her womb: but Rachel was barren.
verses.modern: When the LORD saw that Leah was hated, he opened her womb, but Rachel was barren.

verses.kjv: And Leah conceived, and bare a son, and she called his name Reuben: for she said, Surely the LORD hath looked upon my affliction; now therefore my husband will love me.
verses.modern: Leah conceived and bore a son. She called his name Reuben, for she said, 'Because the LORD has looked upon my affliction; surely now my husband will love me.'

verses.kjv: And she conceived again, and bare a son; and said, Because the LORD hath heard that I was hated, he hath therefore given me this son also: and she called his name Simeon.
verses.modern: She conceived again and bore a son, and said, 'Because the LORD has heard that I am hated, He has given me this son also.' And she called His name Simeon.

verses.kjv: And she conceived again, and bare a son; and said, Now this time will my husband be joined unto me, because I have born him three sons: therefore was his name called Levi.
verses.modern: Again she conceived and bore a son, and said, 'Now this time my husband will be joined to me, because I have borne Him three sons.' Therefore His name was called Levi.

verses.kjv: And she conceived again, and bare a son: and she said, Now will I praise the LORD: therefore she called his name Judah; and left bearing.
verses.modern: She conceived again and bore a son, and said, 'This time I will praise the LORD.' Therefore she called His name Judah. Then she stopped bearing.

chapters.summary: Jacob arrived in Haran, met Rachel at the well, and agreed to serve Laban seven years for her hand. On the wedding night Laban substituted Leah for Rachel; Jacob discovered the deception in the morning and agreed to serve seven more years for Rachel. The LORD opened Leah's womb because she was unloved, and she bore Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah.

verses.kjv: And when Rachel saw that she bare Jacob no children, Rachel envied her sister; and said unto Jacob, Give me children, or else I die.
verses.modern: When Rachel saw that she bore Jacob no children, she envied her sister. And she said to Jacob, 'Give me children, or I shall die!'

verses.kjv: And Jacob's anger was kindled against Rachel: and he said, Am I in God's stead, who hath withheld from thee the fruit of the womb?
verses.modern: Jacob's anger was kindled against Rachel. He said, 'Am I in the place of God, Who has withheld from you the fruit of the womb?'

verses.kjv: And she said, Behold my maid Bilhah, go in unto her; and she shall bear upon my knees, that I may also have children by her.
verses.modern: Then she said, 'Here is my servant Bilhah; go in to her, so that she may give birth on my knees. I too may have children through her.'

verses.kjv: And she gave him Bilhah her handmaid to wife: and Jacob went in unto her.
verses.modern: So she gave him her servant Bilhah as a wife, and Jacob went in to her.

verses.kjv: And Bilhah conceived, and bare Jacob a son.
verses.modern: Bilhah conceived and bore Jacob a son.

verses.kjv: And Rachel said, God hath judged me, and hath also heard my voice, and hath given me a son: therefore called she his name Dan.
verses.modern: Then Rachel said, 'God has judged me, and has also heard my voice and given me a son.' Therefore she called His name Dan.

verses.kjv: And Bilhah Rachel's maid conceived again, and bare Jacob a second son.
verses.modern: Rachel's servant Bilhah conceived again and bore Jacob a second son.

verses.kjv: And Rachel said, With great wrestlings have I wrestled with my sister, and I have prevailed: and she called his name Naphtali.
verses.modern: Then Rachel said, 'With mighty wrestlings I have wrestled with my sister and have prevailed.' So she called his name Naphtali.

verses.kjv: When Leah saw that she had left bearing, she took Zilpah her maid, and gave her Jacob to wife.
verses.modern: When Leah saw that she had stopped bearing, she took her servant Zilpah and gave her to Jacob as a wife.

verses.kjv: And Zilpah Leah's maid bare Jacob a son.
verses.modern: Then Leah's servant Zilpah bore Jacob a son.

verses.kjv: And Leah said, A troop cometh: and she called his name Gad.
verses.modern: Leah said, 'Good fortune has come!' So she called his name Gad.

verses.kjv: And Zilpah Leah's maid bare Jacob a second son.
verses.modern: Leah's servant Zilpah bore Jacob a second son.

verses.kjv: And Leah said, Happy am I, for the daughters will call me blessed: and she called his name Asher.
verses.modern: Leah said, 'Happy am I! For women have called me happy.' So she called his name Asher.

verses.kjv: And Reuben went in the days of wheat harvest, and found mandrakes in the field, and brought them unto his mother Leah. Then Rachel said to Leah, Give me, I pray thee, of thy son's mandrakes.
verses.modern: In the days of wheat harvest Reuben went and found mandrakes in the field and brought them to his mother Leah. Then Rachel said to Leah, 'Please give me some of your son's mandrakes.'

verses.kjv: And she said unto her, Is it a small matter that thou hast taken my husband? and wouldest thou take away my son's mandrakes also? And Rachel said, Therefore he shall lie with thee to night for thy son's mandrakes.
verses.modern: But she said to her, 'Is it a small matter that you have taken away my husband? Would you take away my son's mandrakes also?' Rachel said, 'Then he may lie with you tonight in exchange for your son's mandrakes.'

verses.kjv: And Jacob came out of the field in the evening, and Leah went out to meet him, and said, Thou must come in unto me; for surely I have hired thee with my son's mandrakes. And he lay with her that night.
verses.modern: When Jacob came from the field in the evening, Leah went out to meet him and said, 'You must come in to me, for I have hired you with my son's mandrakes.' So he lay with her that night.

verses.kjv: And God hearkened unto Leah, and she conceived, and bare Jacob the fifth son.
verses.modern: God listened to Leah. She conceived and bore Jacob a fifth son.

verses.kjv: And Leah said, God hath given me my hire, because I have given my maiden to my husband: and she called his name Issachar.
verses.modern: Leah said, 'God has given me my wages because I gave my servant to my husband.' So she called His name Issachar.

verses.kjv: And Leah conceived again, and bare Jacob the sixth son.
verses.modern: Leah conceived again and bore Jacob a sixth son.
